correctness.rationale: For B=L−iκ|w><w| the norm derivative is −2κ|<w,ψ(s)>|². The dark space is the sum of the parts of each L-eigenspace orthogonal to w and reduces B; on its orthogonal complement every eigenvalue of −iB has negative real part, so finite-dimensional Jordan blocks also decay. In the five-class quotient write v=(v_w,x,a,b,y), c=n−1−m and ℓ(v)=a−x+b+cy. The displayed matrix gives ℓ(Mv)=mℓ(v)+m(m−n)y. The first four Krylov columns have (w,X,b,Y) minor t² from the successive pivots 1,−1,t,−t; ℓ kills those columns, and its value on M⁴e₁ is −mt(m−n). Replacing the a row by ℓ and moving it past b,Y preserves the determinant, proving −mt³(m−n). At balance the stated d is trap-zero, satisfies Ld=md and has the asserted norm; the nonzero minor rules out any further dark direction inside S. The class-constant projector gives the bridge, ordinary-site, and mixed-state formulas including the t>0 and κ>0 restrictions. Replay: RESULT.md lines 23–48 plus the row functional above.
